                                                                  ♥ Acknowledgements ♣




            ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
   The first and biggest thanks go to Emily Abell, who not only gave
   me the time and space to write this but who designed the cover with
   the help of stock resources by kjpargeter and writerfantast.
      Nate Meyvis, who co-hosts the Thinking Poker Podcast with
   me, is my best poker buddy. He’s a big part of the reason I still find
   the game fun and interesting, and he’s shaped the way I think and
   talk about it more than anyone else.
      The other people who continually rekindle my passion for poker
   are Carlos Welch and Tommy Angelo. They are the two happiest
   people I know, and I’m so glad that we were able to parlay their
   guest appearances on my podcast into genuine friendships. They’ve
   contributed to this book in both tangible and intangible ways.
      I’m grateful to the others who discussed the manuscript with
   me, read drafts, and offered valuable feedback: Brenna Warren,
   Breyer Calvert, Eric Keppler, Eric Liebeler, Graham Stuart, Kelley
   Slay, Josh Nixon, Sean Lango, and Steve Leahy.
      The most daunting part of this process was wrapping my head
   around the publishing process, and Alex Fitzgerald, Barry Carter,
   Douglas Stewart, Ed Miller, and Zach Elwood were all very helpful
   with that.
      It’s impossible to thank by name every person who contributed
   to this book. I’m grateful to everyone who’s ever talked poker with
   me, to the authors of all the books I’ve read and the producers of
   all the strategy videos I’ve watched, to my students, and to all the
   guests we’ve had on the Thinking Poker Podcast.
      A lot of professionals complain that their families don’t
   understand or approve of poker, but I’ve never known anything
   but support from mine. This is one of the smaller things for which
   I’m grateful to my parents.

♦ Play Optimal Poker ♠

   My father, brother, grandmother, and grandfather were my
original home game, and now I have great fun playing poker with
my cousins Henry, Oliver, and Walter. My Uncle Tubby was my
first backer, at a Florida dog track when I was about five years old.
That doesn’t make him sound like a very good uncle, but he was
the best.

                                                                    ♥ About the Author ♣


                ABOUT THE AUTHOR
   Andrew Brokos’s professional poker career began in 2004, when he
   graduated from the University of Chicago with a B.A. in philosophy.
   He initially played small-stakes online games to make ends meet
   while searching for jobs at education-oriented non-profit
   organizations but quickly saw that taking poker seriously could
   produce enough income to start his own non-profit.
      Later that year, Andrew founded the Boston Debate League and
   served as volunteer executive director until 2008, when the
   organization was large enough to hire a full-time director.
      Since then, Andrew has dedicated himself full-time to teaching
   and playing poker. He currently makes instructional videos for
   Tournament Poker Edge and Red Chip Poker and writes a monthly
   column for Two Plus Two Magazine.
      In 2012, Andrew Brokos and Nate Meyvis launched the
   Thinking Poker Podcast, a weekly show that quickly became one of
   the most popular poker podcasts on the internet. You can find the
   podcast archives and more information about private coaching at
   www.thinkingpoker.net.
